page: Google Cloud Platform n2-highcpu-8 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance featuring 8 vCPUs and 8 GB of RAM, resulting in a 1.0 GB memory-per-core ratio. Powered by an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor running at 2.8 GHz, the instance allocates 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The CPU architecture includes a 33 MB L3 cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 KB L1d cache. It features hardware support for AVX, AVX512F, AVX512_VNNI, AES cryptography, and BMI2 instruction sets. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and has zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data indicates average multi-core CPU performance, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 7430.34 and a PassMark CPU score of 8305.34. Memory bandwidth is average, reaching 412.9 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 48.32 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. However, single-core performance is weak, as evidenced by a stress-ng single-core score of 1409.67 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1138.0. Software compilation with Clang and text processing perform at average levels, whereas tasks like ray tracing, image processing, and physics simulations fall into the bottom 25% tier.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the n2-highcpu-8 offers a dense allocation of dedicated compute cores relative to its memory footprint, making it suitable for compute-bound workloads that do not require large memory capacities. It is well-suited for workloads such as static web serving, software compilation, basic database operations, and lightweight LLM inference using small models. It is less suitable for memory-intensive applications, heavy image processing, or complex physics simulations due to its low RAM-to-vCPU ratio and weaker single-core performance.
description: Google Cloud Platform n2-highcpu-8 is an x86_64 compute-optimized virtual machine featuring 8 dedicated vCPUs and 8 GB of RAM, powered by a 2.8 GHz Intel Xeon processor. It lacks local storage and bundled GPUs. Performance benchmarks show average multi-core CPU capabilities, static web serving throughput, and software compilation speeds, though single-core execution and memory-intensive operations are relatively weak. With a low 1 GB RAM per vCPU ratio, this instance is qualitatively cost-efficient for compute-heavy, memory-light tasks. It is best suited for workloads such as static web serving, software compilation, text processing, and lightweight machine learning inference using small models.
